content.text:
Both are top-tier schools, and their IB exam results are now close. The real differences are the curriculum route, how mixed the student body is, how much you pay, and which side of the city you'd live on.

## At a glance

| | **BIS Hanoi** (British International School) | **UNIS Hanoi** (United Nations International School) |
|---|---|---|
| **Founded** | 2012 | 1988, the first international school in Vietnam |
| **Ownership** | Run for profit by Nord Anglia Education, a large global school group | Non-profit, founded with UN support; one of only two UN international schools in the world (the other is in New York) |
| **Location** | Vinhomes Riverside, Long Bien (east of the Red River) | Ciputra, Tay Ho (northwest Hanoi), about 10 km from the centre |
| **Campus** | Modern, purpose-built | 9.2 ha, the largest school campus in Hanoi |
| **Curriculum** | English National Curriculum and IPC in primary, then IGCSEs (UK exams at 16), then the IB Diploma or the school's own BIS Hanoi Diploma | IB at every stage: PYP (primary), MYP (middle years), then the IB Diploma |
| **Ages** | 2–18 | 3–18 |
| **Student mix** | 30+ nationalities, but mostly Vietnamese and Korean (about 50% and 35% in the school's 2022–23 secondary profile) | 60+ nationalities and 40+ home languages, a more evenly spread expat and diplomatic community |
| **Size** | Smaller | About 1,100 students |

## Fees for 2026–27 (VND, per year, tuition only)
These figures are from VnExpress's May 2026 survey.

| Stage | BIS | UNIS |
|---|---|---|
| Kindergarten | about 511–524M | about 460–708M |
| Primary | about 658–735M | about 878M |
| Secondary | about 847–970M | about 927M–1.05 billion (the highest in Hanoi) |
| One-off fees | 4.5M application, 23.6M registration (Foundation Stage) or 70.8M (Primary and above), 23.6M deposit | about 15.8M registration, 35.5M tuition deposit (USD 1,500), 44.5M enrolment |

UNIS sets its fees in USD. Paying by semester adds 4%, and paying the full year early gets a small discount. **Overall, UNIS costs roughly 10–20% more than BIS at most stages.**

## IB Diploma results (school average vs. world average)

| Year | BIS | UNIS | World |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | — | 32.25 | 30.3 |
| 2025 | 33.24 | 34.0 | 30.58 |
| 2026 | 35.11 (two perfect scores of 45) | 35.42 | 30.88 |

Both schools are well above the world average and nearly tied. UNIS has a larger IB group (about 73 diplomas in 2025) and a strong bilingual diploma rate (39% in 2025), which reflects how many languages its students speak. BIS also publishes strong IGCSE results: in 2025, 46% of grades were A* or A, against 23% in England.

## How to choose

**Choose BIS if you:**
- Want a British-style structure with IGCSEs, especially if a move back to the UK or Commonwealth is likely
- Live on the Long Bien / Vinhomes Riverside side
- Want lower fees, or value Nord Anglia extras like the Juilliard music partnership and the Global Campus
- Are comfortable with a student body that is mostly Vietnamese and Korean

**Choose UNIS if you:**
- Want an IB education from start to finish, or are likely to move between countries, since IB schools exist worldwide
- Want the most internationally mixed peer group in Hanoi and a UN-linked, non-profit ethos
- Live in Tay Ho or Ciputra (where many expats live), or value the large campus and facilities
- Can afford the highest fees in the city

**The practical deciding factor is often the commute.** The two campuses are on opposite sides of the Red River, and Hanoi traffic makes a cross-city school run hard. Visit both, ask how many places are available in your child's year group, and check what happens to students who need English or learning support.

Sources: VnExpress International (2026–27 fee survey), BIS Hanoi / Nord Anglia results pages and 2026–27 fee schedule, the UNIS Hanoi Annual Report and fees page, and WhichSchoolAdvisor. Fees change every year, so confirm them directly with each school.
